problem: Prove a variance-scaled bound on the normalized Turán deficit δ_D at the first-descent index D of a Poisson-binomial pmf, establishing that V·δ_D ≥ 1/4 when V ≥ 1.
debate: Log-concavity and Turán inequalities in Poisson-binomial distributions; related to Darroch's modal localization and the cubic mass inequalities of Hillion and Johnson.
gap: Prior work (Darroch, variance-scaled bounds, cubic inequalities) controls modal location and maximal mass separately but does not compare the normalized Turán deficit with variance; whether V·δ_D is uniformly bounded away from zero was open.
contribution: Proves Theorem 1.1 (V·δ_D ≥ 1/4) and Proposition 1.2 (infimum c* satisfies 1/4 ≤ c* ≤ 1/3), combining normalized-mass bounds, lattice bounds, and exact Bernstein expansions to close the gap.
note: Technically solid, clearly scoped for ECP, with genuine novelty in variance-scaled Turán inequalities and computer-assisted proof methods.
